question: Which animal is the FASTEST on Earth?

post.premise: The fastest animal alive is not the one on land
post.bait: The cheetah is not even close.
post.sources_line: Guinness World Records; Cornell Lab of Ornithology; National Geographic; U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service

youtube.title: What is the fastest animal in the world? Not the cheetah 🏎️

Which one did you pick?

threads.text: Which animal is the fastest on Earth — cheetah, sailfish or peregrine falcon? One of them has been clocked at more than three times motorway speed, the record was measured with a skydiver alongside, and it nearly went extinct sixty years ago.

intent: The land-speed trap: everyone says cheetah, but the peregrine's hunting dive triples it — shown as speed blocks against a motorway car, a falcon rising out of the US where the record was measured, and a city-to-city pin pair for the comeback.

research.topic: Fastest animal: peregrine falcon (Falco peregrinus) — hunting stoop recorded at 389 km/h (242 mph) by falconer Ken Franklin's bird 'Frightful' diving alongside a skydiver over Washington State (National Geographic, 1999–2005); cheetah ~112 km/h (fastest land animal); peregrine populations crashed from DDT in the 1950s–60s, removed from the US endangered species list in 1999, now nesting on skyscrapers and bridges in cities worldwide

myths.myth: The cheetah is the fastest animal on Earth.
myths.reality: The cheetah is the fastest land animal (~112 km/h); the peregrine falcon's hunting dive, recorded at 389 km/h, is more than three times faster and is the fastest speed of any animal.

landscape.our_gap: Speed Shorts are top-10 lists with stock footage; nobody asks it as a quiz, puts the speeds next to a motorway car on a map, and tells where the record was measured and how the bird came back from near-extinction.
